text:
incident-bot: 🚨 Pager fired: dedicated-tenant=orpheus-cluster alert_id=PD-7890 severity=P1
incident-bot: reason=reserved_capacity_throttle, symptoms=95th_latency>1200ms, error_rate~5%, queue_depth spike > 300
PagerDuty: Notification sent to oncall (Mia) and primary escalation (Alex)
Mia: acked PD-7890, pulling graphs now. tagging @Jordan for kv-cache hints.
Mia: quick snapshot — reserved pool utilization at 98%, per-GPU qps high, some workers in backpressure.
Sam: seeing repeated KV eviction logs for tenant orpheus: "kv_cache_evict key=chat_prefix reason=mem_pressure" last 1m ~ 420/s
Jordan: hmm that matches a recent workload change — they pushed longer chats. KV hit ratio down to 0.62.
Mia: any immediate low-risk mitigations?
Jordan: yes — two options: 1) temporarily bump reserved capacity by +2 gpus (fast but costs), 2) enable tenant fallback to shared pool (riskier for latency). Runbook: /runbooks/dedicated/tenant-throttle.md
Mia: doing quick safety check with capacity controller. running:
```
# dry-run: propose bump
./infra/capacity adjust --tenant orpheus --delta 2 --dry-run
```
Mia: dry-run looks OK, no scheduling constraints on region eu-west-1.
PagerDuty: auto-escalated to Alex after 2m without resolution.
Alex: on it, liaising with infra to push +2 GPUs and open a transient burst window. @CSM-Eve FYI — will update customer SLO impact.
Sam: also recommend quickly enabling prefix KV caching TTL extension for orpheus to reduce churn. patch queued:
```
PATCH kv-service: set ttl=8h for tenant=orpheus
```
Mia: applying TTL patch (can rollback). executing now.
Mia: TTL patch applied — monitoring for reduced evictions.
Jordan: evictions down ~70% in 30s, queue depth trending down.
Mia: infra confirms capacity +2 scheduled, estimate ~4m to spin up.
Mia: temporarily throttling non-critical routes for orpheus (rerank/analytics) to free tokens.
Alex: confirmed capacity added, routing updated, latency 95th back to ~280ms, error rate down to 0.6%. still above baseline but acceptable for now.
CSM-Eve: notifying customer about transient degradation and mitigation steps. sending note now.
Mia: moving to monitoring→post-incident review. will keep thread open for handoff.
Alex: leaving a follow-up action: investigate long-term kv cache sizing and autoscale thresholds for orpheus. assigned to Jordan.
Mia: handing off to next oncall @Alex in 30m for watch — set reminder for RCA and cost approval for added GPUs.
PagerDuty: PD-7890 status: acknowledged by Mia, escalated to Alex, resolved (mitigated) by resource bump + TTL patch.
incident-bot: incident ticket created: INC-2023-orf-042, severity=P1 — link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2023-orf-042
Mia: closing active page, leaving ops notes in the incident ticket. Good catch team. :thumbsup:
Alex: received handoff, will follow up during daytime.
